meta.location: The city of Zarahemla; the valley of Gideon

world_behind.title: Eight verses of minutes, attached to a sixty-two-verse sermon
world_behind.text: Alma 5 is what he said; this is what happened next. Ordinations, admissions, removals, a standing rule about attendance, an instruction about fasting, and a departure. The record almost never shows the administrative sequel to a sermon, and here it gives one in full.

world_behind.title: Both directions in consecutive verses
world_behind.text: Verse 2 admits outsiders who repented. Verse 3 removes insiders who did not. Nothing separates the two sentences, and the chapter offers no commentary on the symmetry.

world_behind.title: Removal takes the name and leaves the seat
world_behind.text: Verse 3 blots names out of the register; verse 5 keeps the meetings open to everyone regardless. The discipline is documentary. A person whose name has been struck off the roll is still entitled to be in the room.

world_behind.title: The congregation is pointed outward immediately
world_behind.text: Verse 6 has them gathering oft and joining in fasting and mighty prayer, in behalf of the welfare of the souls of those who knew not God. The assembly that has just expelled its proud members is set to praying for people outside it.

world_behind.title: A name that will not stop carrying its murder
world_behind.text: Verse 7 explains the valley, then the city, then names them both after Gideon, then adds who killed him and how. This is the third time Nehor is named in six chapters, and the record has still not stopped citing the sword.

world_behind.title: Four warrants, and nobody is arguing
world_behind.text: Verse 8 gives Alma's authority to preach at Gideon four separate times over before he says a word. There is no opponent anywhere in the chapter, no challenge to answer, and the sentence piles up credentials anyway.

world_behind.title: The chapter closes like a document
world_behind.text: "And thus it is written. Amen." The formula turns up once in this record and twice in the New Testament, and in every case it marks the end of a citation rather than the end of an argument.

words.text: To sit at the head of. The verb appears once in this record and five times in the Old Testament, and here it is paired with something softer: priests and elders ordained to preside and watch over the church. Two duties, one about position and one about attention.

Thrown back, refused. The verse applies it to members who would not repent, and it does so before the names come off the list. The removal is the consequence. The word is strong and the procedure it describes is quiet.
Taken away from someone who had a claim to it. The word is unique in this record. What none were deprived of is the privilege of assembling to hear, a narrower thing and a deliberately chosen one.

Often, frequently, an adverb without a number attached. Treated at 1 Nephi 18:3. The command is to gather oft, which is looser than the one day in every week that Alma's father had set apart at the waters of Mormon. When the Lord gives the same instruction at Bountiful centuries later he uses this same word and no number either.

Rules made for the running of a thing. The noun appears four times in this record and never in the Bible, and this is the only place it names church practice rather than civil government. Whatever Alma did in verses 1 through 6, the record files it as administration.

Something uncovered. The verse specifies what was revealed: the truth of the word spoken by his fathers. It is confirmation of old content, the same claim he made about himself at the end of the sermon.

phrases.text: The method, given in six words, with no ceremony described. Paul told Timothy his gift came by the laying on of the hands of the presbytery, and Luke reports the apostles doing it after prayer. This record treats it as procedure.
Two verbs for one arrival, and the second is passive. They were baptized; they were received. Somebody did the receiving. Admission is an act of the congregation.

phrases.term: Their names were not numbered among those of the righteous
phrases.text: A list, and the consequence of coming off it. Alma had used the same clause in the sermon a chapter earlier, of the wicked; the same practice runs from Mosiah's church at Zarahemla to Moroni's account at the very end of the record. What changes here is who is being counted out.

phrases.term: The word of God was liberal unto all
phrases.text: An odd sentence, because the adjective belongs to people. Generosity is being credited to the message rather than to anyone dispensing it, which takes the decision about access out of the hands of whoever is standing at the door.

phrases.term: In behalf of the welfare of the souls
phrases.text: The stated object of the fasting, and it is entirely external. Not for the congregation's own healing, not for the members recently removed, but for people who have never been inside. The instruction arrives three verses after an expulsion.

phrases.term: Being called after the man who was slain by the hand of Nehor
phrases.text: A place name given its full provenance for the second time in the book. The valley was explained in almost these words four chapters ago, and the record explains it again anyway, adding the city that has since been built there. Some names are not allowed to become just names.

phrases.term: According to the testimony of Jesus Christ, the Son of God
phrases.text: The third of the four warrants, and the only one that is not about Alma. The others are things in him or given to him; this one names a person he is testifying about, and the clause that follows says what that person came to do.

phrases.term: And thus it is written. Amen.
phrases.text: Four words ending a chapter that had no argument to close. The formula belongs to citation. It is how you finish quoting a source, and here it is applied to a piece of church minutes, which quietly makes the minutes a document worth citing.

verses.label: v. 1
verses.title: An ordination reported as procedure
verses.text: The record describes the act by its mechanism and its purpose rather than by its significance: "he ordained priests and elders, by laying on his hands according to the order of God, to preside and watch over the church." Three things are specified, the physical act, the standard it follows, and the duty conferred. Nothing is said about who was chosen or how many, and the verse is the only account the chapter gives of how the leadership came to exist.

verses.label: v. 4
verses.title: A whole institution summarised in one clause
verses.text: The record closes the administrative section with a sentence that reports no event: "thus they began to establish the order of the church in the city of Zarahemla." Began is doing the work, since nothing is said to be finished. The verse marks the ordinations and the two movements of verses 2 and 3 as the establishment itself, so the church is described as constituted by a procedure rather than by a founding moment.

verses.label: v. 5
verses.title: Access stated as a rule, and it is unrestricted
verses.text: One verse sets out who may attend: "the word of God was liberal unto all, that none were deprived of the privilege of assembling themselves together to hear the word of God." The clause is universal and carries no qualification of belief, membership, or conduct. It sits immediately after two verses about people being received and blotted out, so the record distinguishes between belonging to the church and being allowed into the room.

verses.label: v. 6
verses.title: A members-only practice, and its object is outsiders
verses.text: The one restricted activity in the chapter is described in the same breath as its purpose: "the children of God were commanded that they should gather themselves together oft, and join in fasting and mighty prayer in behalf of the welfare of the souls of those who knew not God." Membership determines who does the fasting; non-membership determines who it is for. The record puts the two clauses side by side and adds no comment on the arrangement.

verses.label: v. 7–8
verses.title: The chapter ends by moving the subject somewhere else
verses.text: The last two verses report a departure and a destination: "when Alma had made these regulations he departed from them, yea, from the church which was in the city of Zarahemla," and then "Alma went and began to declare the word of God unto the church which was established in the valley of Gideon." The phrase made these regulations names what the preceding six verses were, and the record uses it as the reason the man is now free to leave.

chapter.title: This is the paperwork, and the record keeps it
chapter.text: Five administrative acts follow in six verses: ordination "by laying on his hands according to the order of God" at verse 1; admissions at verse 2; removals at verse 3, where names "were blotted out"; an open-access rule at verse 5, "none were deprived of the privilege of assembling themselves together"; and a standing instruction at verse 6 to "gather themselves together oft, and join in fasting and mighty prayer." The roll moves in both directions in consecutive verses, and the chapter exists to record what the sermon of Alma 5 produced.

chapter.title: The two doors are worked in the same paragraph
chapter.text: People come in at verse 2 and people go out at verse 3, and the record neither celebrates the one nor laments the other. Membership is being treated as something with an actual boundary that traffic crosses in both directions.

chapter.title: Discipline is documentary, and the room stays open
chapter.text: The names come off a list. The privilege of assembling to hear does not come off with them. That distinction, between belonging to a body and being allowed to be present, is drawn in two verses and never argued for.

chapter.title: A congregation that has just purged itself is told to pray for outsiders
chapter.text: The natural motion after expelling the proud is inward: consolidate, examine, recover. Verse 6 sends them the other way, and names the beneficiaries as people who knew not God.

chapter.title: Generosity is credited to the word
chapter.text: Verse 5 credits the generosity to the message itself. Whoever is standing at the door is thereby not the one deciding how far it opens, which is a striking thing to write in the chapter that has just recorded who was thrown out.

chapter.title: Gideon's name is not allowed to go blank
chapter.text: Fourth chapter in, the valley was explained. Here it is explained again, with the city added, and the killer named a third time. A place name is being kept from becoming ordinary, one restatement at a time.

chapter.title: Authority is stacked where nobody is challenging it
chapter.text: Four warrants stacked without a break, in a chapter with no opposition in it. The stack is not a defense; it is a description of what the man thinks he is carrying when he walks into a new town.

chapter.title: Role in the book
chapter.text: Alma 6 closes the Zarahemla section and opens the circuit. From here the pattern is fixed: arrive, declare, and move on. The next chapter is the Gideon sermon this one ends by introducing.

applications.title: Do the paperwork after the sermon
applications.text: Ordinations, admissions, removals, a written rule. Whatever was moving in the room during a great meeting will be gone by Thursday unless somebody records what changed and who is responsible for what.

applications.title: Keep the door open to people you have removed
applications.text: A name came off a list; nobody was barred from the room. If a boundary is worth having, it is worth drawing narrowly enough that the person on the wrong side of it can still hear what you have to say.

applications.title: Name the grounds precisely
applications.text: Not "wickedness" but those lifted up in the pride of their hearts, who would not repent or humble themselves. Discipline stated in general terms is discipline nobody can answer or appeal.

applications.title: Point the fast outward
applications.text: They gathered and fasted for people who did not know God. Communal attention naturally turns toward the community's own wounds; this instruction spends it on strangers.

applications.title: Credit the generosity to what you are carrying
applications.text: The word was liberal to all. Anyone who thinks of themselves as the one being generous has already put a hand on the door.

applications.title: Say who slew him
applications.text: The record names the killer every time it names the valley. Softening how a thing happened, once it is a place name and a habit, is how a community forgets what it learned.

applications.title: Know what you stand on before you arrive
applications.text: Four warrants, listed before a word is preached at Gideon and with nobody disputing any of them. Being clear about the basis you act on is worth doing when you are not under attack, because that is when you can think.

questions.text: When someone came back, was I the one who received them, or did I leave that to somebody else?
Could I state the grounds for a judgment I have made about someone, precisely enough for them to answer it?
Whose access am I quietly rationing on my own authority?
When did I last fast, pray, or go without for somebody outside my own circle?
What have I let become just a name, that used to mean something specific?
If I had to list what I am standing on, could I?
